title: Existence of K-injective resolutions of sheaves of modules
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site whose underlying category is small (its objects form a set) and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Then the abelian category $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] (it has all colimits, filtered colimits are exact, and $\bigoplus_{U\in\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal C}j_{U!}\mathcal O_U$ is a generator, where $\mathcal O_U$ is the restriction of $\mathcal O$ to the localized site $\mathcal C/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] and $j_{U!}\mathcal O_U$ is the sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the extension-by-zero presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $P_{\mathcal O_U}$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]), and every cochain complex $\mathcal M^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] admits a K-injective resolution [def-pur-kinjective-complex] $\mathcal M^\bullet\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ which is injective in every degree [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and which can be chosen functorially in $\mathcal M^\bullet$ (a functor $\mathcal M^\bullet\mapsto\mathcal I^\bullet$ on the category of complexes with a natural transformation from the identity whose components are such resolutions).

source.place: Section 07A5 (sites-cohomology-section-unbounded), first paragraph: Mod(O) is Grothendieck abelian (Modules on Sites, Section sites-modules-section-kernels, Lemmas sites-modules-lemma-j-shriek-flat, sites-modules-lemma-module-quotient-flat) and literature/stacks-project/injectives.tex Theorem 079P (injectives-theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck)

proof.text: The category of sheaves of modules on a small ringed site is Grothendieck abelian, with the stated colimits, exact filtered colimits, and generator, by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian].

source.place: Section 07A5, first paragraph; Modules on Sites, Lemmas 03DA, 03DB, 03EW

proof.text: Apply the functorial K-injective resolution theorem [lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence] to the Grothendieck abelian category from Step 1. Its functor I and natural transformation eta give, for every cochain complex M, a quasi-isomorphism M \to I(M) with K-injective target and injective terms in every degree; the functoriality is exactly naturality of eta and the action of I on chain maps.

split_report.summary: Split the proposition into the general small ringed-site Grothendieck theorem and the functorial K-injective resolution theorem with injective terms. The proof then applies these two statements to Mod(O), preserving the item's generator, degreewise injectivity, and functoriality clauses.
